answer: Persistent compute thread. Each identity must continuously solve a small proof-of-work tied to its public key, chaining outputs so the work cannot be precomputed or copied. Cloning forces the attacker to run a fresh compute thread per identity at full cost, while honest agents pay the same once and keep it. Verification is a light whisper of sampled checkpoints, not full replay. Because the chain grows like a slow glacier, abandoned or duplicated identities decay and lose standing. Attacker cost: full compute per clone, no shortcut.
